title: File record
description: A files asset that a pipeline declares in [files]: a file, a folder of files or a glob of them, whatever is inside. ChartBook does not read it. Other fields the manifest declares for it (sources, providers, license, restrictions...) are carried as they are.

ref.description: The record's address as named fields: the same address as `id`, with nothing to parse.

pipeline.description: The ID of the pipeline that declares the asset.

path.description: As declared in chartbook.toml, relative to the pipeline's root: a file, a folder, or a glob.

resolved_path.description: Absolute path on the machine that built the index. Absent from a published index.

modified_at.description: When the file, or the newest of its files, was last written, in UTC. Absent when not built.

content_hash.description: Hash of the asset's content: of its file, or of the listing of its files. Absent when its path matches no file.

size_bytes.description: The size of all its files together.

file_count.description: How many files it is: 1 for a path that names one file. Absent, with `content_hash`, when the path matches no file, a folder with none in it included.

extensions.description: How many of its files there are of each type, the most common first: by the end of their names in lower case (`.jsonl.gz`, `.pdf`; an ending of digits alone, as `.1` of a rotated log, is passed over; `` for none). The 20 most common are named, and the files of every other type are counted under `other`.

files.description: Its first 1000 files, sorted by path; `file_count` says how many there are. A path that names one file lists that file, by its name.

path.description: Relative to the folder, or to the glob's fixed prefix, with forward slashes.

partitions.description: The keys of the `key=value` folders it is in, and their values, as text.

keep.description: The manifest marks this asset `keep = true`: every version of its bytes is kept in the store (`store gc` keeps, for each, the newest snapshot holding it), and `chartbook restore` puts it back on disk. Present only when it does.

docs.description: The write-up: the file it is in, or the text itself when it was written inline.

content_hash.description: The hash of the write-up's text, so a build says which text it showed. Write-ups are not pinned; the commit holds them.
